questions_and_answers.question_text: What is rúguǒ one of the commonest words for?
Which other word is widely used for "if"?
May the idea of "if" be conveyed without any special word?
Write the Chinese question meaning "How much time does it take to go from Sānlǐtún to the airport?"
Write the Chinese for "It takes forty minutes."
Write the Chinese for "If I leave home at eight o'clock, I can make it in time. Right?"

answers.answer_text: Rúguǒ wǒ bādiǎn zhōng líkāi jiā, láidejí ba?

questions_and_answers.question_text: What does líkāi mean, and what may follow it?

answers.answer_text: "To leave" — it may be followed by an object (the place).
A district in Běijīng where many foreign diplomats and Chinese people from other countries live.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give an example of "if" conveyed without a special word.

answers.answer_text: Bādiǎn zhōng líkāi jiā láidejí ba? — "If I leave home at eight o'clock, I can make it in time, right?"

articles.text:
5. A: Cóng Sānlǐtún dào fēijīchǎng   How much time does it take to go
      yào duōshao shíjiān?            from Sānlǐtún to the airport?
   B: Yào sìshifēn zhōng.             It takes forty minutes.

6. A: Rúguǒ wǒ bādiǎn zhōng líkāi     If I leave home at eight o'clock, I
      jiā, láidejí ba?                can make it in time. Right?
   B: Láidejí.                        Yes.

Note on No. 6

Rúguǒ is one of the commonest words in Chinese for "if." Another widely used word for "if" is yàoshi. You have already learned that the idea of "if" may be conveyed in Chinese without any special word:

Zuò Gōnglùjú děi xiān mǎi        If I take the bus, is it necessary
piào ma?                         to buy tickets ahead of time?
Bādiǎn zhōng líkāi jiā           If I leave home at eight o'clock,
láidejí ba?                      I can make it in time. Right?
